title: CochleaNet: deep learning analysis of cochlear connectomics and gene therapy
summary: The journal abstract describes CochleaNet, a deep-learning framework for cleared-cochlea light-sheet images, covering hair cells, spiral ganglion neurons, synapses, tonotopy and gene expression. Trained on mouse data, it was applied to gerbil and lower-resolution mouse and marmoset data. The authors say they analyzed neuron types and validated gene-therapy products but the abstract does not identify the biological or therapy-comparison findings. The date represents the 2026-10-23 journal version; an earlier preprint appeared on 2025-11-17.
ai_technology: CochleaNet: deep learning framework for volumetric image segmentation and analysis
organization: University Medical Center Göttingen; University of Göttingen

evidence.tested: Manual-analysis and prior-segmentation comparisons; applications to neuron types, gene-therapy products, gerbil cochleae and lower-resolution mouse and marmoset imaging. The abstract does not state the specific biological outcomes.
evidence.unknown: The journal abstract reports neuron-type analyses and gene-therapy-product validation without stating their specific biological or product-comparison outcomes. Complete Methods and Results, sample sizes and the distinction between tool validation and biological or therapeutic validation were not assessed. This omission does not establish that the paper contains no qualifying finding.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning framework that reconstructs the cochlea and segments hair cells, neurons and synapses, and quantifies tonotopy and gene expression.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary Molecular Therapy journal abstract and metadata, and the author-institution page reproducing the 2025 preprint abstract. Complete primary Methods and Results were not accessed; journal and preprint evidence were kept version-specific.
